system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: production cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure) at work
G2: production on-call
G3: cluster administration
G4: CKA certification (not yet passed)
G5: Terraform at work

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Listing CKA or Terraform Associate as held certifications
T2: Claiming AWS/GCP production experience or 'managed Kubernetes clusters'
T3: Presenting homelab tools (Argo CD, Prometheus, Terraform) as work experience

# OUTPUT 1: CV
MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
DevOps / Platform Engineering | QA Automation Engineer
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including the last two focused primarily on
CI/CD pipelines, test environments and build tooling. Owns GitLab CI pipelines for three product
teams and has built merge-request ephemeral environments on a shared Kubernetes cluster.
Experienced in improving pipeline performance, infrastructure automation, observability for test
metrics, and cross-team technical documentation. Building further infrastructure-as-code and
Kubernetes experience through a personal k3s and Terraform project.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
CI/CD and build tooling: GitLab CI, Jenkins, pipeline optimization, artifact publishing
Containers and orchestration: Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes (namespace-level access;
basic), k3s
Infrastructure as code and automation: Terraform (personal project), Ansible (basic), Bash, Python
Observability and data: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, PostgreSQL, SQL
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Operating systems and version control: Linux, Git
Cloud learning: AWS EC2 and S3 basics (personal free tier)
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software | Wroclaw
2021–Present
• Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (approximately 25 developers), covering build,
unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, and artifact publishing.
• Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelizing test jobs, caching
dependencies and separating end-to-end tests into their own stage; monthly CI runner costs fell by
about 30%.
• Built merge-request ephemeral environments comprising an application, PostgreSQL and seeded
data, deployed via Helm to the shared Kubernetes cluster from GitLab CI; environments are
automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
• Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the
flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.
• Built a Python and PostgreSQL pipeline-results workflow and Grafana dashboards to show flaky
tests by team.
• Wrote Bash and Python tooling to seed test data in PostgreSQL.
• Wrote the internal guide to CI pipelines used in team onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023.
QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House | Wroclaw 2019–2021
• Tested web and mobile applications for client projects using manual and automated testing.
• Introduced a Selenium and Java automated regression suite for the largest client project.
• Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.
Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House 2018–2019
• Investigated customer issues in logs and databases and reproduced bugs for developers.
SELECTED PROJECTS
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal 2024–2025
• Built a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster; deploys applications from a Git repository using
Argo CD.
• Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, with Traefik ingress and cert-manager for
TLS.
• Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level.
Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health 2023–2024
• Delivered short-lived application and PostgreSQL environments with seeded data for each merge
request, deployed with Helm to the shared Kubernetes cluster from GitLab CI.
• Set environments to be destroyed automatically after merge or 48 hours of inactivity, enabling QA
and product review before merge and end-to-end testing against the environment.
Flaky Test Dashboard | Odrava Health 2023
• Collected CI test results in PostgreSQL and built Grafana dashboards showing flaky tests by team.
• The flaky-test rate fell from 7% to below 1% after teams began addressing the leading offenders.
CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health 2022
• Profiled pipelines across three teams, parallelized test jobs, added dependency caching and
separated end-to-end testing into its own stage.
• Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.
EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018
CERTIFICATION AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Currently studying for the Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam; exam scheduled for
January 2027.
LANGUAGES
Polish (native), English (C1), German (A2)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role.
The opportunity to help build infrastructure for Corvale’s new train fleet is especially
compelling because the work connects software delivery with real-world transport systems,
and the platform is being shaped from an early stage.
In my current test-infrastructure role, I own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams and
built merge-request environments deployed with Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster. They
bring together an application, PostgreSQL and seeded data, and are automatically removed
after merge or 48 hours of inactivity. I also improved pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and
reduced monthly runner costs by about 30%. These projects have given me practical
experience making environments repeatable, supporting teams’ delivery workflows and
documenting technical processes clearly.
I am extending that experience through a personal k3s and GitOps homelab, where I use Argo
CD, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Traefik and cert-manager, and provision a small Hetzner
VPS with Terraform. My production Kubernetes work is at namespace level, while the
platform team operates the shared cluster; my Terraform experience is from personal
infrastructure rather than production cloud engineering. I am currently studying for the CKA
exam, scheduled for January 2027.
Corvale’s focus on telemetry, alerting and reliable train-to-cloud services would let me bring
my strengths in automation, observability and practical team support to a consequential
infrastructure challenge while continuing to grow as an infrastructure engineer. I would
welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to the Fleet
Connectivity team.
Kind regards,
Marta Kowal-Brandt

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
